การเว้นวรรค ตามหลักเกณฑ์ที่สำนักงานราชบั: Spacing according to the guidelines set by the Office of the Royal Society
ในการเขียนหรือพิมพ์หนังสือไทย การเว้นช่อ: In writing or printing Thai, correctly leaving spaces between words, phrases or sentences is essential, because it makes the writing accurate, clear and unambiguous, and lets it be read exactly as the writer intended.
วรรค คือ คำ ข้อความ หรือประโยคช่วงหนึ่ง: A วรรค (wak) is a word, phrase or segment of a sentence
การเว้นวรรค หมายถึง การเว้นช่องว่างระหว่: การเว้นวรรค (spacing) means leaving a space between วรรค
– การเว้นวรรคเล็ก มีระยะห่างระหว่างวรรคป: – Small space: a gap between วรรค roughly equal to the width of the consonant ก
– การเว้นวรรคใหญ่ มีระยะห่างระหว่างวรรคป: – Large space: a gap between วรรค roughly 2 times a small space
ในการเขียนหรือพิมพ์หนังสือไทย มีหลักเกณฑ: In writing or printing Thai, the guidelines on spacing are as follows:
๑. กรณีที่ต้องเว้นวรรค: 1. Cases Where a Space Is Required
เว้นวรรคใหญ่เมื่อจบข้อความแต่ละประโยค: Leave a large space at the end of each sentence
(๑) นั่งให้เรียบร้อย อย่าไขว่ห้าง: (1) นั่งให้เรียบร้อย อย่าไขว่ห้าง (“Sit properly. Do not cross your legs.”)
(๒) วิทยาการเป็นต้นธารให้บังเกิดความรู้แ: (2) วิทยาการเป็นต้นธารให้บังเกิดความรู้และความสามารถในอันที่จะประกอบกิจตามหน้าที่ได้ดี ความเจริญงอกงามทั้งทางจิตใจและทางวัตถุย่อมเป็นผลสืบเนื่องมาจากวิทยาการ บ้านเมืองจะเจริญหรือเสื่อมก็เนื่องด้วยวิทยาการ (“Learning is the source of knowledge and the ability to perform one's duties well. Spiritual and material progress both stem from learning; whether a nation prospers or declines depends on learning.”)
เว้นวรรคเล็ก ในกรณีต่อไปนี้: Leave a small space in the following cases
๑.๒.๑ ในประโยครวมให้เว้นวรรคเล็กระหว่างป: 1.2.1 In a compound sentence, leave a small space between clauses that are complete in meaning and joined to other clauses beginning with conjunctions such as “และ” (and), “หรือ” (or), “แต่” (but), etc.
(๑) นายแดงอยู่ที่บ้านคุณพ่อของเขาที่ปากน: (1) นายแดงอยู่ที่บ้านคุณพ่อของเขาที่ปากน้ำโพ แต่พี่ชายของเขาอยู่ที่บ้านซื้อใหม่ในกรุงเทพฯ (“Mr. Daeng lives at his father's house in Pak Nam Pho, but his elder brother lives in a newly bought house in Bangkok.”)
(๒) การเขียนหนังสือโย้หน้าเย้หลังไม่เป็น: (2) การเขียนหนังสือโย้หน้าเย้หลังไม่เป็นระเบียบ หรือการขาดความระมัดระวังในเรื่องช่องไฟ อาจเป็นเครื่องหมายส่อนิสัยของผู้เขียนเองได้ (“Untidy, slanting handwriting, or carelessness with spacing, may reveal the writer's character.”)
(๓) พุทธกับไสย แม้ต่างกันเป็นคนละด้าน แต: (3) พุทธกับไสย แม้ต่างกันเป็นคนละด้าน แต่ก็ไม่เป็นสิ่งขัดแย้งกันในความเชื่อถือของคนชั้นสามัญทั่วไป (“Buddhism and supernatural belief, though different, do not conflict in the beliefs of ordinary people.”)
แต่ถ้าเป็นประโยคสั้นให้เขียนติดกัน: But short sentences are written without a space
(๑) ฉันและเธอไปโรงเรียน: (1) ฉันและเธอไปโรงเรียน (“You and I go to school.”)
(๒) เขาอยากได้ดีแต่เขาก็ไม่ได้ดี: (2) เขาอยากได้ดีแต่เขาก็ไม่ได้ดี (“He wanted to do well but he did not.”)
(๓) น้ำขึ้นแต่ลมลง: (3) น้ำขึ้นแต่ลมลง (“The tide rises but the wind drops.”)
๑.๒.๒ เว้นวรรคเล็กระหว่างชื่อกับนามสกุล: 1.2.2 Leave a small space between a given name and a surname

(๓) ๑๕ ๑๓ ๑๑ ๙ ๗ ๕ ๓ ๑ ต่างก็เป็นจำนวนเล: (3) ๑๕ ๑๓ ๑๑ ๙ ๗ ๕ ๓ ๑ ต่างก็เป็นจำนวนเลขคี่ (“15 13 11 9 7 5 3 1 are all odd numbers.”)

(๑) เขาเจริญพุทธคุณว่า อิติปิ โส ฯลฯ ภคว: (1) เขาเจริญพุทธคุณว่า อิติปิ โส ฯลฯ ภควาติ (“He chanted the virtues of the Buddha: อิติปิ โส … ภควาติ.”)
(๒) วันหนึ่ง ๆ เขาทำอะไรบ้าง: (2) วันหนึ่ง ๆ เขาทำอะไรบ้าง (“What does he do in a day?”)
(๓) อเปหิ = อป + เอหิ: (3) อเปหิ = อป + เอหิ
(๔) กฤษณา : กฤษณาสอนน้อง แบบเรียนกวีนิพน: (4) กฤษณา : กฤษณาสอนน้อง แบบเรียนกวีนิพนธ์ (“Kritsana: Kritsana Teaches Her Sister, a verse textbook”)

หลักเกณฑ์การทับศัพท์ ตามหลักเกณฑ์ที่สำนั: Guidelines on Transliteration according to the guidelines set by the Office of the Royal Society
๑. การทับศัพท์ให้ถอดอักษรในภาษาเดิมพอควร: 1. Transliteration should render the letters of the source language closely enough to show the origin of the word, and should be written in a form that is easy to read in Thai.
๒. การวางหลักเกณฑ์ได้แยกกำหนดหลักเกณฑ์กา: 2. Separate transliteration guidelines have been set for each language.
๓. คำทับศัพท์ที่ใช้กันมานานจนถือเป็นภาษา: 3. Transliterated words that have long been in use, are regarded as Thai and already appear in the Royal Institute Dictionary, continue to be used as before, e.g. ช็อกโกเลต, ช็อกโกแลต (chocolate), เชิ้ต (shirt), ก๊าซ, แก๊ส (gas)
๔. คำวิสามานยนามที่ใช้กันมานานแล้ว อาจใช: 4. Proper nouns that have long been in use may continue to be used as before, for example:
Victoria = วิกตอเรีย: Victoria = วิกตอเรีย
๕. ศัพท์วิชาการซึ่งใช้เฉพาะกลุ่ม ไม่ใช่ศ: 5. For technical terms used only by specialist groups, rather than general vocabulary, additional guidelines may be set as necessary.
ประวัติความเป็นมาของราชบัณฑิตยสภาและสำนั: History of the Royal Society of Thailand and the Office of the Royal Society, from 1926 to the present
จุดเริ่มต้นของราชบัณฑิตยสภา: The Origins of the Royal Society of Thailand
เมื่อวันที่ ๑๙ เมษายน พ.ศ. ๒๔๖๙ พระบาทสม: On 19 April 1926, His Majesty King Prajadhipok, King Rama VII of the Chakri Dynasty, graciously proclaimed the establishment of the “ราชบัณฑิตยสภา” (Royal Society). The King saw fit to revive the work of the Krom Ratchabandit, an ancient department and a position to which those learned in the arts and sciences were appointed to serve the Crown. Later, in 1933, the House of Representatives advised His Majesty King Prajadhipok that a Royal Institute should be established, with members of learning who might in future be elected as Fellows, to carry out research and disseminate knowledge to the public and to produce textbooks widely. His Majesty therefore graciously enacted the Royal Institute Act in 1933 and repealed the proclamation establishing the Royal Society dated 19 April 1926.
เริ่มแรกที่ตั้งราชบัณฑิตยสถานนั้น ยังไม่: When the Royal Institute was first established, there were as yet no Fellows, only Associate Fellows, who held their first meeting in the Grand Palace on 16 June 1934. Later, the Royal Institute Act B.E. 2485 was issued, and the first Fellows were appointed by Royal Command on 30 September 1942, numbering 51 people.
งานสำคัญในช่วงแรกเกิดจากพระราชดำริในพระบ: Key work in the early period arose from the royal initiative of His Majesty King Prajadhipok, namely the annual competition for writing books teaching Buddhism to children, which the Royal Institute has carried on from 1934 to the present. In addition, there are 5 other main areas of work: revising the dictionary, which was originally the work of revising the Pathanukrom transferred from the Ministry of Public Instruction in 1934; the encyclopedia; coining Thai technical terms; the geographical gazetteer; and setting the guidelines for the romanization of Thai.
ที่ทำการของราชบัณฑิตยสถานแรกเริ่มได้ใช้ต: The Royal Institute's premises were first the upper floor of the Somdet residence at Bang Khun Phrom Palace. It later moved to the Thawon Watthu Building, the northern part of the Vajiravudh Library building on Na Phra That Road, until 1988, then to the Ratchawallop Building in the Grand Palace until 2006, when it moved to Sanam Suea Pa, Dusit District, Bangkok, where it remains today.
การดำเนินงานของราชบัณฑิตยสถาน แบ่งเป็น ๒: The Royal Institute's operations were divided into 2 parts: the Council of Fellows and the civil service. The Council of Fellows set policy for academic work and consisted of council members who were Fellows from 3 academies, namely the Academy of Moral and Political Sciences, the Academy of Science and the Academy of Arts. The President of the Royal Institute was President of the Council, the Vice President of the Royal Institute was Vice President of the Council, the Secretary-General of the Royal Institute served as Secretary of the Council, and the Deputy Secretary-General served as Assistant Secretary of the Council. In the civil service part, the Secretary-General of the Royal Institute was head of the agency, assisted by the Deputy Secretary-General, overseeing the academic and administrative work of the Office of the Secretary, the Moral and Political Sciences Division, the Science Division and the Arts Division, and coordinating work with all the academies.
การดำเนินงานด้านวิชาการ ดำเนินงานในรูปขอ: Academic work is carried out through academic committees, which hold meetings to consider terms, coin technical terms, write explanations of terms in various fields and set language guidelines. The results, as bodies of knowledge, are then disseminated to the public through various channels, including print, radio, television and electronic media, so as to meet the public's needs widely. Feedback is also gathered in order to make services more effective.
นอกจากนี้ ราชบัณฑิตยสถานได้จัดทำโครงการเ: In addition, the Royal Institute has run many projects to disseminate knowledge in various fields and to preserve and promote the Thai language, including the “Know and Love Thai” project, a key project under government policy; the ASEAN Languages and Cultures project; and the National Language Policy project. It also exchanges knowledge and coordinates with other learned societies and academic institutions in Thailand and abroad. The Royal Institute has continuously carried out its mission of study, research and the advancement of all branches of knowledge. Its best-known academic work, used as a reference and as the standard for writing Thai, both in official documents and in education, so that usage is uniform, is the Royal Institute Dictionary.
จากราชบัณฑิตยสถานสู่ราชบัณฑิตยสภา: From the Royal Institute to the Royal Society of Thailand
ในปี ๒๕๕๖ ราชบัณฑิตยสภาโดยสภาราชบัณฑิตเห: In 2013, the Council of Fellows considered it appropriate to change the name “ราชบัณฑิตยสถาน” (Royal Institute) to “ราชบัณฑิตยสภา” (Royal Society of Thailand), the original name given by His Majesty King Prajadhipok when he founded it on 19 April 1926, in honour of the 120th anniversary of his birth. It also sought to improve the powers, duties and academic administration of the Royal Society so that its work would reach the national academic community and the general public more widely; to establish a welfare fund for members of the Royal Society for their benefit; and to allow income the Royal Society receives from academic administration and from education and training to be spent on the duties of the Office of the Royal Society without having to remit it to the Treasury as state revenue, giving greater flexibility in academic administration.
ในปี ๒๕๕๘ พระบาทสมเด็จพระเจ้าอยู่หัวได้ม: In 2015, His Majesty the King issued a Royal Command proclaiming that it was appropriate to revise the law on the Royal Institute, and graciously enacted the Royal Society Act B.E. 2558, published in the Royal Gazette, Volume 132, Part 10 Kor, dated 13 February 2015, and in force from 14 February 2015. The name of the agency “ราชบัณฑิตยสถาน” (Royal Institute) was therefore changed to “สำนักงานราชบัณฑิตยสภา” (Office of the Royal Society), and “สภาราชบัณฑิต” (Council of Fellows) was changed to “ราชบัณฑิตยสภา” (Royal Society of Thailand).
Section 6 of the Royal Society Act B.E. 2558 states that the Royal Society of Thailand is an institution for the advancement of all branches of knowledge, founded by His Majesty King Prajadhipok, with the objective of carrying out study and research in order to disseminate, promote and exchange knowledge, and to develop, preserve and provide academic services for the benefit of the country and the people. Under Section 12, the Royal Society of Thailand has 3 types of members: 1. Associate Fellows, 2. Fellows, 3. Honorary Fellows. Section 24 of the Act establishes a council within the Office of the Royal Society, called the “ราชบัณฑิตยสภา” (Royal Society of Thailand), consisting of the President of the Royal Society of Thailand as President of the Council, 2 Vice Presidents of the Royal Society of Thailand as Vice Presidents of the Council, and all Fellows as council members, with the Secretary-General of the Office of the Royal Society serving as Secretary of the Council and the Deputy Secretary-General serving as Assistant Secretary of the Council.
อำนาจหน้าที่ของสำนักงานและราชบัณฑิตยสภา: Powers and Duties of the Office and the Royal Society of Thailand
ในส่วนสำนักงานราชบัณฑิตยสภานั้นเป็นส่วนร: The Office of the Royal Society is a government agency known by another name, with the status of a department not under the Office of the Prime Minister, a ministry or a sub-ministry, under the law on state administration. It has many important powers and duties, such as conducting study and research, advancing all branches of knowledge and disseminating its work for the benefit of the country and the people; producing dictionaries, encyclopedias, gazetteers and taxonomies; coining technical terms in various fields, including compiling dictionaries of foreign-language technical terms in Thai, and other academic work; setting guidelines on the use of the Thai language; preserving the Thai language so that it does not change for the worse; and promoting the Thai language, a hallmark of the nation, so that it becomes ever more prominent.
ส่วนราชบัณฑิตยสภามีอำนาจหน้าที่วางนโยบาย: The Royal Society of Thailand has the power and duty to set policy for academic work within the powers and duties of the Office of the Royal Society; to consider and approve rules and regulations on the operations of the Royal Society; to elect the President and Vice Presidents of the Royal Society of Thailand; and to resolve to approve nominations for the appointment of Fellows and Honorary Fellows.
นับตั้งแต่วันที่ ๑๔ กุมภาพันธ์ พ.ศ. ๒๕๕๘: Since 14 February 2015, the agency “ราชบัณฑิตยสถาน” (Royal Institute) has been renamed “สำนักงานราชบัณฑิตยสภา” (Office of the Royal Society), and “สภาราชบัณฑิต” (Council of Fellows) has been renamed “ราชบัณฑิตยสภา” (Royal Society of Thailand), but academic work and services disseminating its work to the public continue, along with development to meet the public's needs more widely and quickly. Besides producing academic books in various fields, radio and television programmes, CDs and DVDs disseminating knowledge, and e-learning materials, in 2015 the Office of the Royal Society made its most-demanded books more usable by engaging the National Electronics and Computer Technology Center (NECTEC) to develop applications of the Royal Institute Dictionary B.E. 2554 and of How to Read and How to Write, Royal Institute edition, for use on smartphones. The Office of the Royal Society and NECTEC have also agreed to cooperate in turning other academic works into applications. In addition, the Office of the Royal Society has improved and promoted Thai-language learning for people with disabilities, for example by producing Braille editions of the Royal Institute Dictionary and How to Read and How to Write for people with visual impairments, and by holding training in correct Thai pronunciation for blind people and teachers of the blind, so that people with visual impairments and blind people can learn correct Thai pronunciation on an equal footing with others.
นอกจากนี้ สำนักงานราชบัณฑิตยสภายังมีโครง: The Office of the Royal Society also runs a project to build a database of words in the Royal Institute Dictionary, and promotes the preservation of local dialects and local wisdom in every region of the country by compiling knowledge on the dialects of the North, the Northeast and the South and disseminating it through printed books, radio programmes and competitions in which students tell stories of pride in their home communities in their local dialect.
หน้าที่ภารกิจและบทบาทสำคัญของสำนักงานราช: The duties, mission and key roles of the Office of the Royal Society — creating knowledge in various fields, setting standards for the use of the Thai language and improving academic services to the public — have been carried out and developed continuously over the 90 years since the founding of the Royal Society of Thailand on 19 April 1926 to the present.
